_comment: One honest line per paper saying what she lost, shown in red on the progress page. Keyed by <subject>/<exam-folder>. Where there is no entry the site falls back to pulling a sentence out of the marking report, which is rougher. Add a line here after each marking.
chemistry/exam-26-ch11p1-rev8: Half a mark on Q.4(iii): wrote "it is emitted directly" where she meant "is NOT emitted directly". One dropped word inverted the answer.
chemistry/exam-25-ch10-rev6-8: Q.7 reversed the reaction and reused the worked example's value instead of re-deriving it, and Q.9(ii) left a mole result with no unit.
chemistry/exam-23-ch10-rev4-6-8-9: Section C was the loss: incomplete equations and missing state symbols, plus the conclusion habit returning.
chemistry/exam-22-ch1-9: A missing minus sign on an exponent, and three re-set errors from exam-21 that had not yet stuck.
chemistry/exam-21-ch1-9: Written work was perfect at 16/16. Everything lost was in the MCQ section, on confusable pairs.
islamiat/exam-05-bab3b-retest: Q.2(iii) missed the five things the book says to avoid, and one reference was still missing: Sahih Bukhari 4315.
islamiat/exam-04-bab3b: Zero references across six pages on a paper that asked for them three times, and the eight-mark answers were headings with one line each.
islamiat/exam-03-bab1-2-3-4-6-7: Lost marks where the answer named a thing but gave no incident, date or reference to go with it.
quran/exam-03-naml-hajj: Q.4 asked about Hajj and qurbani and she answered only qurbani. Across the whole paper she wrote one surah name and no ayah numbers.
quran/exam-02: All five lost marks sat in Section B, and shared one cause: the question asked for teachings and the answer retold the story.
physics/exam-17-ch7p1-rev3-6: Q.5(vi) named tungsten from memory when the question said to use Table 7.1, where the answer is gold. Half a mark more for writing "flowing" as an arrangement.
physics/exam-16-ch1-6-9: Three half-marks for recording slips: a wrong unit, a value copied wrongly, and one missing concluding sentence.
physics/exam-15-ch1-6-9: One mark, on a question she knew. Her best paper of the year at that point.
biology/exam-18-ch1-7: Two marks: the H of NADPH left off, and lymphatic confused with immune for the second time.
biology/exam-17-ch1-7: Two equation slips, and one difference explained in the wrong direction.
math/exam-19-ch6-10-11: Q.6 on probability was not attempted at all, the single largest loss. Unit 6 was untaught and still came out perfect at 11/11.
math/exam-18-ch1-2-4-5-7: Q.3 was skipped because her numbering slipped, and one log law was named loosely.
